summary: The cause of the two 20 s window freezes is unknown, so these tests prove the window now records any main-thread block of 500 ms or more: one capped log line per block naming its duration, start and context, with a fake observer and a fake clock; and any backend command of 100 ms or more: one capped log line naming the command and its duration, with a fake clock.

tests.name: longTask > a block counts from 500 ms; shorter or broken durations do not
longTask > a 20 s block becomes one record naming its duration, start and context
longTask > the limiter lets 5 records through per minute and counts the rest as dropped
longTask > a 20 s freeze leaves exactly one record with the right fields
longTask > a storm of long blocks is capped, and the cap opens again after a minute
LAG-04A wiring > the window starts the long-task watch at load
LAG-04A wiring > the record goes to the app log through the existing boot_timing command
